subject: Immediate: p95/p99 latency uplift after model-split rollout - BlackOak Labs
messages:
From: Jordan Price <ops@blackoak.ai>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@blackoak.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: sudden p95/p99 uplift after today's model-split rollout

Hi team,

We started seeing a noticeable jump in p95 and p99 tail latency around 08:45 PT after your teams rolled the model-split / A-B variant (model-v3b-quant) into our hosted endpoint. Our throughput is steady but error rate is climbing (5xxs rising from ~0.1% to ~1.4%) and a handful of requests are timing out at 30s. Attached is a sample latency graph and the small trace dump we collected.

This is customer-impacting — several internal workflows are timing out and blocking ingestion. Can you confirm whether this rollout included a change to caching/kv access or serving kernel changes? We need an immediate mitigation plan or rollback ETA.

Jordan
SRE, BlackOak Labs
Attachments: blackoak_p99_uplift_20270614.png, trace-samples-06-14.txt

- Karthik's team will pull live traces and check KV cache hit-rate + kernel path selection.
- We’ll gate the A variant and roll traffic back to model-v2 for BlackOak if we confirm regression.
- I’ll keep you updated every 15m until we have a mitigation.

Can you paste one example request id from the trace-samples file (x-request-id) so we can correlate?

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: sudden p95/p99 uplift after today's model-split rollout

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jordan Price <ops@blackoak.ai> wrote:
> We started seeing a noticeable jump in p95 and p99 tail latency around 08:45 PT after your teams rolled the model-split / A-B variant (model-v3b-quant) into our hosted endpoint.

Quick triage notes (first-pass):
- Observed a spike in KV cache miss ratio for the affected endpoint coincident with canary promotion (approx +28% miss).
- Model-v3b-quant path is hitting a different kernel that increases per-token latency at long contexts (>512 tokens). BlackOak's traffic has many >700-token requests.
- A small number of requests show repeated retriable 502s originating at the batching layer under load.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Gate traffic: rollback traffic for BlackOak to model-v2 (target rollback window: 3–5 mins) — low-risk and reversible.
2) Temporarily widen SLO thresholds and increase per-VM concurrency to reduce queuing while rollback proceeds.
3) Post-rollback: we’ll run a synthetic suite against long-context prompts to reproduce and identify kernel mismatch.

I’m preparing a rollback plan now and will request a controlled traffic shift at 09:46 PT unless we see objection.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Jordan Price <ops@blackoak.ai>

Thanks — request-id examples: r-7f8c2b9a and r-7f8c3d4e are in the trace-samples file.

We approve a rollback. ETA: we need confirmation within 10 minutes. Also please confirm whether rollback affects any in-flight jobs; we have a scheduled nightly batch at 11:30 that must not be impacted.

Jordan

P.S. We’d like an interim post-mortem (high level) for leadership after stabilization.

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Price <ops@blackoak.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T09:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: sudden p95/p99 uplift after today's model-split rollout — rollback complete & next steps

Jordan — rollback executed at 09:55 PT (traffic shifted back to model-v2 for BlackOak). Immediate observations:
- p95 returned to baseline within two minutes; p99 back to normal within six minutes.
- Error rate dropped from ~1.4% down to 0.12%.
- No indication of stuck in-flight jobs; the traffic shift was graceful with connection draining. Nightly batch at 23:30 unaffected.

Next steps (owners/timeline):
- Karthik/Hannah: reproduce in staging with long-context suite and isolate kernel mismatch (24–48h).
- Rohan: collaborate with BlackOak SRE to collect targeted traces and confirm no data loss (today, <3h).
- Marissa/Ben: prepare an executive summary + customer-facing note and credit recommendation (by EOD).

We’ll assemble a short incident summary and share a post-mortem draft by EOD tomorrow. Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll treat this as high priority.

— Rohan Mehta
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
